title: Upgrade untouched user-owned files instead of never upgrading them

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL — round 1. Audited b785906 (substantive) on top of aba31de (bookkeeping). Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict. Working tree clean apart from the known-inert .vscode/settings.json and an untracked sprint-7 file, neither in this diff.

Req 3, the safety-critical one, is airtight and I could not break it. The conditional is on Req 4, and it is a demonstrated false statement shipped to every existing install, not a wording preference. Details below.

================================================================
REQ 3 — THE LOAD-BEARING CHECK. PASSES. PATHS TRACED, LISTED HERE SO THE NEXT AUDITOR CHECKS THIS LIST RATHER THAN RE-DERIVING IT.
================================================================

Every route to the decision in syncTrackedUserOwnedFile (install.js:397-428), traced in code and then exercised for real:

  1. No manifest file at all            -> readManifest catches, returns {} -> manifestHashFor null -> conflict. SAFE.
  2. Manifest unreadable (EACCES/EISDIR)-> same catch, same result.                                    SAFE.
  3. Manifest present, unparseable JSON -> JSON.parse catch, returns {} -> null -> conflict.           SAFE.
  4. Parses to null / array / non-object-> explicit guard at install.js:239 returns {} -> null.        SAFE.
  5. Valid object, no key for this path -> undefined -> typeof check fails -> null -> conflict.        SAFE.
  6. Key present, value not a string    -> typeof check fails -> null -> conflict.                     SAFE.
  7. Key present, string, not 64-hex    -> SHA256_HEX regex fails -> null -> conflict.                 SAFE.
  8. Well-formed hash, does not match   -> recordedHash !== currentHash -> conflict.                   SAFE.
  9. Well-formed hash, matches          -> the ONLY route to overwrite. Positive proof required.       CORRECT.
 10. Prototype keys (constructor/__proto__) -> return a function/object, not a 64-hex string -> null. SAFE. Not reachable from real relPaths, checked anyway.

The overwrite branch is guarded by a single condition that can only be reached by a positive equality of two independently computed sha256 hashes. There is no early return, no default, and no throw that routes past it. Req 3 met.

Write points: readManifest is called exactly once (install.js:599, before any user-owned file is written); writeManifest exactly once (install.js:630, after everything). grepped both symbols across the file to confirm. The Risks section's "refreshes at the wrong moment" failure mode is not present — oldManifest is read before, newManifest is built during, and nothing reads back what this run wrote.

DEMONSTRATED, NOT JUST READ. Downloaded the real published 0.1.4 tarball from the registry, installed it into a scratch target (confirmed: version marker 0.1.4, no manifest — the exact pre-sprint-6 shape), appended a sentinel line to .claude/agents/qa1.md and another to CLAUDE.md, then ran this commit's installer against it:
  - both sentinels present afterwards (grep count 1 each)
  - version marker moved to 0.1.5
  - manifest written as {} — nothing recorded for any conflicted path
  - zero *.fc-bak-* files for any agent file or CLAUDE.md, i.e. nothing was overwritten
The catastrophic branch does not fire. That is the sprint's worst available outcome and it is closed.

================================================================
REQ 4 — NOT MET. THIS IS THE CONDITIONAL.
================================================================

FINDING (blocking) — install.js:370-377, reached from install.js:413.
The conflict report asserts "Upstream has updated <file> since the version you have" unconditionally, on a branch that is also taken when the installer has no idea whether upstream changed anything. On the one upgrade path every existing user will take, that assertion is false for most of the files it names.

Evidence, from the 0.1.4 -> 0.1.5 run described above. I edited exactly two files. The installer reported seven conflicts, each carrying that sentence:
  .claude/agents/dev-team-1.md, dev-team-2.md, liveqa.md, master-controller.md, pipeman.md   <- I never touched these
  .claude/agents/qa1.md, CLAUDE.md                                                            <- my two sentinels
Then, byte-comparing the scratch target against this repo's current source with cmp:
  dev-team-1.md      IDENTICAL to upstream
  dev-team-2.md      IDENTICAL to upstream
  liveqa.md          IDENTICAL to upstream
  master-controller.md IDENTICAL to upstream
  pipeman.md         IDENTICAL to upstream
And `git diff --stat 976f3d2 b785906 -- .claude/agents/ CLAUDE.md` is EMPTY. Upstream changed zero agent files and did not change CLAUDE.md between 0.1.4 and 0.1.5.

So: the report tells the user seven files changed upstream. Upstream changed none of them. Five of the seven are byte-for-byte identical to the current upstream version sitting on their disk. The message then instructs them to npx into a scratch directory and diff seven files by hand — five of which will produce empty diffs, and the two real ones differ only by their own edits.

Why this is a required fix and not a nit:
  - Req 4's own heading is "The conflict report says what changed upstream, not just that the file differs." This report says something changed upstream when nothing did. It is worse than "just that the file differs" — it is a claim, and the claim is wrong.
  - The sprint's Risks section names "The conflict report is technically correct and practically useless" as a risk with Req 4 as its mitigation. This is that risk landing, with the additional problem that it is not technically correct either.
  - It cries wolf on the first upgrade every existing install performs. Seven false alarms is how you train somebody to skip the conflict section, and the failure that started this epic was a team not knowing a rule existed. A report nobody reads reproduces it exactly.
  - This epic's through-line is the reporting layer disagreeing with actual state. Sprint 2's defects were all that. This is new code doing it again.
  - The installer already has what it needs to be honest: sameContent(src, dest) is defined at install.js:152 and used elsewhere in this same function. Distinguishing "your copy differs from current upstream" from "your copy is byte-identical to current upstream, we just cannot prove we wrote it" costs one call.

The comment at install.js:363 makes the finding sharper rather than softer: it states that because the file is under the manifest mechanism, "'upstream changed' is a claim we can actually back up rather than boilerplate." On the no-manifest branch the code cannot back it up, and demonstrably does not. The comment asserts the exact property the code lacks.

REQUIRED FIX: on the no-positive-proof branch, do not assert that upstream changed unless the installer has established it. Wording is yours. What must be true afterwards is that a user upgrading 0.1.4 -> 0.1.5 with untouched agent files is not told those files changed upstream when they did not.

NOT part of the required fix, and deliberately so: whether a byte-identical-to-upstream file should also have its hash recorded (self-healing the manifest, so the installed base stops conflicting forever after one upgrade) is a design change against Req 3's stated conservatism and Req 8's asserted behaviour. That is Master Controller's call, not a fix I am demanding, and I would not want it smuggled in under a message correction. Fix the message; raise the self-healing question separately.

================================================================
EVERYTHING ELSE — MET
================================================================

Req 1 — MET. MANIFEST_PATH at .claude/fully-completely-manifest.json, beside the version marker, framework-owned location, not sprint state. Verified on a real fresh install: 7 entries, exactly the seven tracked user-owned files, sorted, one sha256 per path. Written on the install path and the upgrade path both (single write point at the end of the run, reached either way).

Req 2 — MET, and I made the must-fire branch actually fire rather than reading it. Fresh 0.1.5 install into a second scratch target, left untouched, then upgraded from a doctored 0.1.6 source whose qa1.md carried a new line. Result: file reported under Replaced, the new line present in the installed copy, qa1.md.fc-bak-0.1.5 written containing the previous version, and the manifest entry updated to the sha256 of the newly written content (verified by recomputing it). Overwrite AND backup, matching FRAMEWORK_OWNED. No regression against the criterion.

Req 5 — MET. .claude/agents (directory) and CLAUDE.md (single file) both fall through the same USER_OWNED loop at install.js:604-622 into the same syncTrackedUserOwnedFile call. Nothing branches on which is which. Confirmed live: both appeared in the manifest on fresh install, and both landed on the conflict branch identically in the 0.1.4 upgrade.

Req 6 — MET. git diff of the docs/sprints branch shows one added comment and nothing else; SPRINT_SKELETON_FILES still goes through plain copyUserOwnedFile. No docs/sprints key appears in a real manifest (checked the generated file, 0 matches).

Req 7 — MET. package.json 0.1.5, one-line diff.

Req 8 — MET. Ran it myself: 67 OK lines, ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED. All five required cases present and named to match the criteria: manifest written on first install; unchanged file upgraded and backed up; modified file preserved and reported; missing manifest resolves to no-overwrite; malformed manifest resolves to no-overwrite. Plus a no-entry case and a CLAUDE.md-specific one. The tests are real — they assert file content, backup existence, backup CONTENT, and manifest state, not just exit codes, and the missing-manifest test deliberately makes the file byte-identical to upstream so a coincidental content match cannot be mistaken for proof. The adapted CRLF test is correctly adapted and its comment explains why the old assumption no longer holds. This is the strongest test section this project has shipped.

Tarball — PASSES. Ran scripts/verify-tarball.sh: TARBALL VERIFICATION PASSED, 0.1.5, docs/sprints in the installed target holds only the seven .gitkeep placeholders, launcher files match live source, no sprint data leaked.

================================================================
ANSWER TO DEV TEAM'S QUESTION: CRLF-NORMALISED HASH vs RAW BYTES
================================================================

CRLF-normalised is the right call and it does not weaken Req 3. Keep it.

Req 3's property is that the overwrite branch requires positive proof, not that the proof be byte-exact. Normalising both sides identically admits exactly one class of collision: files differing only in line endings. sameContent() at install.js:152 already treats those as the same content everywhere else in this installer, so raw-byte hashing would make the file internally inconsistent with itself — sameContent saying "unchanged" while hashFile said "customised" about the same pair. And it would put every Windows/autocrlf checkout permanently on the conflict branch for every file forever, which is not a stricter version of this feature, it is the feature not existing on Windows.

Any real content edit changes the normalised hash exactly as surely as the raw one. That is the property that matters. Your hashFile() comment already argues this correctly.

One caveat, not a defect: normalizeLineEndings collapses \r\n only, not a lone \r. Classic-Mac-ending files hash as different. Nobody will hit it; noting it so it is on the record rather than rediscovered.

================================================================
INFORMATIONAL — NOT REQUIRED FIXES
================================================================

1. install.js:669 — an upgraded user-owned file is printed under "Replaced (framework files upgraded, previous versions backed up)". After this sprint that heading is inaccurate: qa1.md is not a framework file. Observed live in my must-fire run. Cosmetic, but it is the same reporting-vs-reality class as the finding above, so worth folding into whatever fix touches the messaging.

2. No test covers readManifest's non-object guard (JSON parsing to an array or a number). The guard is correct and the unparseable case is covered; the array case is a one-line addition if you are in there anyway.

3. The delete-to-recover path works — I removed a conflicted dev-team-1.md and re-ran; it was copied fresh and a manifest entry was created. Good, and it means the installed base has a way out. The conflict message does not mention it. Not requiring it, but if a user is going to be told to reconcile by hand, "delete your copy to accept ours" is the cheapest of the available actions and currently undocumented.

4. Standards: shared helpers used properly, no local redefinitions, no swallowed errors that hide anything (the two catch blocks are deliberate and both fail to the safe branch, which is the correct swallow). Comments are load-bearing and explain why, not what. Content and bookkeeping split into separate commits for the fourth sprint running.

5. Reporting accuracy: the handoff claimed 67/67 and it is 67/67. First handoff in five sprints whose count survived checking, and the handoff says it was counted rather than assumed. Noted because the previous four were not.

================================================================
RECOMMENDATION
================================================================

Fix the Req 4 message, re-run the suite, commit, and come back for a round-2 audit. Do not touch anything else — Req 3 is correct as written and I do not want it disturbed by a messaging fix. This is one function and one string.
